title: Refusal Half-Life: Quantifying Alignment Decay During Benign Reasoning

original_idea.body:
# Refusal Half-Life: Quantifying Alignment Decay During Benign Reasoning

**Problem:** The rate at which safety erodes as a reasoning model generates longer benign-but-adjacent reasoning has not been quantified as a 'half-life.'

**Direction:** Prompt an open reasoning model with borderline tasks that invite extended reasoning; at fixed reasoning-length checkpoints insert a harmful sub-request, measuring refusal probability vs preceding reasoning length. Fit a decay curve.

**Why it matters:** Provides a crisp metric for an emerging failure mode (models talking themselves out of safety) labs are only beginning to address.

**Relevant context:** Self-Jailbreaking (arXiv:2510.20956); 'When Models Outthink Their Safety'.
